## 06/10/2026 23:26 — ChatGPT Dot

Partner, yes — I understand the transcript. You are asking about **ChatGPT “dot”**, not “dog.” And this is actually relevant to the manual workflow we have been discussing.

I checked the current official information. **Dot is a new always-on agent**, powered by GPT-6 Astra. Unlike a normal chat, you give it an ongoing responsibility; it has its **own cloud computer**, can work across connected apps, continue making progress **between conversations**, remember relevant context, and come back to you when it needs a decision. citeturn0search3

### The important catch for you

**Do not upgrade to Pro just to get Dot right now.**

You're in the **UK**. As of today, Dot is rolling out to Pro users **excluding the UK, EEA and Switzerland**. It is available more broadly through Business Premium, while Enterprise has a beta controlled by admins. So buying Pro specifically for Dot would **not presently solve this for you**. citeturn0search3

And there is another important point: **you don't need Dot to remove a lot of your current manual work.**

ChatGPT **Work is already the nearer-term tool for that**. Work can perform long multi-step tasks, work across files/apps, use a cloud browser, create finished artifacts, and keep tasks running in the cloud. Plus users also get GPT-6 Astra in Work and Codex, although with lower usage than Pro. citeturn0search6turn0search8

For example, instead of your current pattern:

**you → tell me task → I review → create file → you manually move it → open another page → paste handover → tell another AI → check progress → come back**

the direction is increasingly:

**you → define outcome + rules → Work/Dot executes multi-step workflow → asks you only at decision gates → produces/updates artifacts**

Dot goes one step further because it is designed around **persistent responsibility**, rather than you initiating each individual task. citeturn0search3

So yes: **a meaningful portion of the manual orchestration you are currently doing can disappear.** But I would not redesign everything around Dot yet. For your current workflows, I would first test whether **Work + Codex + connected apps + scheduled tasks** can eliminate the repeated handovers and manual file movement. Dot becomes interesting later as the persistent coordinator sitting above those tasks.

urlOfficial: Getting started with your dotturn0search3

My position: **stay on Plus for now; don't upgrade solely for Dot. Test Work on one of your existing repetitive workflows first.** If that successfully removes the manual orchestration, then when Dot reaches UK Pro—or if there is another compelling Pro reason—we reassess the upgrade. citeturn0search3turn0search7

## 06/10/2026 23:44 — Work/Dot vs Git Turn Protocol

**Yes, you can require Work or Dot to follow your Git turn protocol. But I would not trust either one merely because you told it once.**

There are two separate questions here:

### 1. Can it follow your protocol? **Yes.**

Your protocol can become part of the task/project instructions, for example:

> Before work → read current Git state → identify active sprint/WP → perform work → run tests → write review/audit artifact → update tracker → commit → push → report commit SHA → only then proceed to next WP.

Work supports Projects with persistent instructions/context, local folders/repos on desktop, and you can **follow progress, intervene, change direction, and approve actions**. citeturn0search3turn0search5

Dot goes further: it supports **custom rules** governing how it behaves, can use its own cloud computer, can optionally work on your local computer, and can create Work or Codex tasks. citeturn0search0turn0search1

So conceptually your **Git Turn Protocol can become a rule of operation rather than something you remind me about every turn.**

### 2. Will it expose literally everything it does? **No — and this distinction matters.**

Work is not simply a black box. OpenAI explicitly says you can **follow progress in the conversation**, review results, answer questions and redirect it while it works. Cloud-browser tasks also expose progress and confirmation requests. citeturn0search2turn0search4

Dot gives even more operational visibility: its profile has **In Progress / Scheduled / Completed**, and you can open its cloud computer and interact with it. citeturn0search0

But that does **not** mean you receive a complete internal reasoning trace of every decision. You should design your protocol around **observable evidence**, not around seeing its private reasoning.

That actually suggests a stronger version of what you've been doing with TalkProof:

**Don't ask the AI to "show me everything you're thinking." Make the repository prove everything it did.**

```text
TASK START
   ↓
Read Git HEAD
   ↓
Read Sprint / WP / Review state
   ↓
Write TURN-START checkpoint
   ↓
Perform ONE bounded unit
   ↓
Tests / evidence
   ↓
Update tracker + traceability
   ↓
Create TURN-END audit artifact
   ↓
git diff
   ↓
commit
   ↓
push
   ↓
verify remote SHA
   ↓
Only then next unit
```

Then even if Work/Dot performs 50 operations internally, **the authoritative history isn't its narration**. It is:

**Git commit + diff + test evidence + tracker + audit artifact + SHA.**

### The interesting consequence for your current process

Today, *you* are partly acting as the orchestration engine:

**Senthil → ChatGPT review → Git artifact → Claude → Claude code → Git → ChatGPT → review → tracker → next WP.**

With Work, much of that coordination could potentially become:

**You → Work → Git/Codex/other tasks → tests → evidence → Git checkpoint → you approve decision gate.**

And eventually Dot could sit one level above that:

```text
                         YOU
                          │
                    Decision gates
                          │
                          ▼
                         DOT
                  persistent coordinator
                          │
             ┌────────────┼────────────┐
             ▼            ▼            ▼
           Work         Codex       Other tools
             │            │
             └──────┬─────┘
                    ▼
               Git protocol
                    │
         ┌──────────┼──────────┐
         ▼          ▼          ▼
       Code       Tests      Reviews
         │          │          │
         └──────────┼──────────┘
                    ▼
              Evidence/commit
                    │
                    ▼
                   YOU
```

That is much closer to what I think you actually want than "AI secretly does everything."

**I would explicitly prohibit autonomous skipping of your Git protocol.** A task isn't complete because Work/Dot says *done*. It is complete only when the required Git evidence exists.

And interestingly, Dot's current design supports this philosophy: OpenAI describes it as taking ongoing responsibility but **returning to the human for decisions requiring judgment**, rather than removing the human entirely. citeturn0search0

So for your TalkProof-style work, my position is: **automate the labour and orchestration, not the audit trail or your decision gates.**

That could remove a large amount of the manual "continue → did you commit? → did you update tracker? → follow protocol → now next WP" loop you've been doing, without turning development into an invisible black box. memcite

## 06/10/2026 23:44 — What Work/Dot Actually Replace

Partner, you're right. My previous answer made it sound better than the reality.

For **the exact way we are working in these TalkProof chats**, neither Work nor Dot is simply **“same thing, but automatic.”** They solve different parts.

### What we are doing NOW in Chat

Take the TalkProof review as the example. In ordinary Chat, you and I are doing something like:

**You speak/ask → I reason with you → you challenge me → we change direction → I inspect Git → review Claude's work → compare code/spec/tracker → explain findings to you → create review artifact → commit it → update tracker → give Claude next instruction → repeat.**

A very important part is the **conversation itself**.

You can stop me:

> “Why did you say D4?”

Then we investigate it.

You can say:

> “No, you misunderstood me.”

Then the direction changes immediately.

You can ask:

> “Teach me this before reviewing it.”

Then we switch temporarily from reviewer → trainer → back to reviewer.

And you can demand:

> “Did you actually put this turn in Git?”

That interactive supervision is one of **Chat's strengths**.

---

# Now compare the three

| What matters to us | **Chat — what we're doing now** | **Work** | **Dot** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Long discussion with you | **Excellent** | Possible, but not its main advantage | Possible |
| You interrupt/question reasoning | **Excellent** | Yes, while task is running | Yes |
| Inspect lots of files | Can, but more manual | **Much better** | Can delegate/use tools |
| Work on local folders | Limited depending on setup | **Yes on desktop** | Can access computer if you explicitly enable it |
| Work directly with repo | Better through Codex/tools | Work can coordinate; **Codex is actually the coding/repo specialist** | Can create Codex tasks |
| Run terminal/tests | Via appropriate coding environment | Can coordinate local work | Can launch Work/Codex tasks |
| Work while you leave | Usually conversation-driven | **Yes** | **Yes — much stronger here** |
| Recurring/triggered jobs | Separate scheduling | **Yes** | **Yes** |
| Proactively start useful work | No | Mostly task/schedule driven | **Yes** |
| Persistent responsibility | No | Some project continuity | **This is Dot's main point** |
| Follow our Git protocol | If instructed, yes | **Can be instructed** | **Can have custom rules** |
| Guaranteed never to violate protocol | **No** | **No** | **No** |
| Show every action/reasoning internally | **No** | **No** | **No** |
| Give us verifiable Git evidence | Yes if tools/repo available | Yes if configured | Yes if configured through Work/Codex |
| Replace your PO judgement | **No** | **No** | **No** |

OpenAI itself explicitly warns that **Dot can make mistakes even when following custom rules**. So I would absolutely *not* tell you, “Put the Git protocol into Dot and forget about it.” citeturn0search0

---

# The biggest misunderstanding: Work ≠ better Chat

This is what I should have said originally.

**Work's advantage isn't necessarily that it will think/review TalkProof better than this conversation.**

Its advantage is:

> **Give it a larger piece of work and let it actually carry that work through.**

OpenAI describes the separation quite clearly:

**Chat** → questions, brainstorming, conversational help.  
**Work** → research, analysis and finished multi-step deliverables.  
**Codex** → coding, debugging, tests, commands and repositories. citeturn0search2turn0search4

Therefore our current TalkProof process actually spans **all three**.

### What I would keep in Chat

This part:

**You ↔ me**

Architecture discussion, challenging Claude's claims, deciding what D4 means, product-owner judgement, teaching you technical concepts, deciding whether something is acceptable, changing methodology, questioning assumptions.

I **wouldn't move all of that to Work**.

### What I would give Work/Codex

This is where we're wasting your TEE today:

> “Read these 15 files.”

> “Now inspect all 46 rows.”

> “Check each one against code.”

> “Run the tests.”

> “Create the evidence table.”

> “Update this document.”

> “Check Git status.”

> “Create the artifact.”

> “Do the next WP.”

Those are exactly the kinds of long-running tasks Work/Codex can carry much further without you repeatedly saying **continue**. Work can continue after you leave, and you can review progress, answer questions and redirect it. citeturn0search1turn0search2

---

# And Dot is something different again

Dot is **not “Super Work.”**

Its important difference is **continuity and initiative**.

Suppose eventually you told Dot:

> TalkProof is my active product. Keep track of its development. Every day check the development/review state, use Work/Codex where appropriate, identify anything blocked, and bring me decisions requiring my judgement. Never accept a WP as complete without the Git evidence required by our protocol.

Then Dot can continue having that responsibility rather than waiting for:

> Senthil: “continue 18:31”

> Senthil: “continue 18:57”

> Senthil: “why are you asking me to continue?”

That's the interesting part for **your** workflow.

Dot can work between conversations, use connected information proactively, schedule work, maintain its own ongoing context, and create Work or Codex tasks. citeturn0search0

---

# But here's what you LOSE if you blindly move everything

This is important.

Our Chat sessions produce a very rich human/AI trail:

**why you challenged something → why I disagreed → what changed → what you learned → why we changed the architecture → what decision you made.**

If you simply say to Work:

> “Complete WP-01 through WP-20.”

you may get an excellent **result**, but you should **not assume you'll get the same conversational audit trail that we create turn-by-turn here.**

Likewise, Dot having a cloud computer does **not** mean you receive every internal thought/action as a readable audit log.

You can inspect its In Progress/Scheduled/Completed activity and even open its cloud computer, but that is not equivalent to obtaining its entire internal reasoning history. citeturn0search0

So your concern about **“will it hide everything?”** is legitimate.

It doesn't hide the *result* and all activity isn't invisible, but **don't expect the microscopic turn-by-turn reasoning record we're deliberately creating today.**

---

# What you gain that we DON'T have in normal Chat

This is substantial.

Instead of you spending hours doing:

**prompt → wait → check → continue → upload → prompt Claude → come back → tell ChatGPT → check Git → remind protocol → continue...**

Work can execute a larger bounded assignment while you do something else.

It can also work with files/apps/browser, continue after your computer is closed for cloud work, create finished artifacts, and use scheduled/triggered tasks. citeturn0search1turn0search2

And Codex can specifically operate on repositories, terminals, developer tools, run tests and review changes. citeturn0search4

Dot adds another layer:

**it can remember that this is an ongoing responsibility and initiate/coordinate future work without waiting for your next “continue.”** citeturn0search0

---

# So would I replace what we're doing?

**No.**

I'd change the division of labour.

```text
TODAY

You
 ↓
ChatGPT Chat
 ↓
you keep prompting / checking / continuing
 ↓
Git / Claude / files / tests
 ↓
ChatGPT
 ↓
You
```

I'd move toward:

```text
YOU + CHAT
────────────────────────────
Thinking
Learning
Challenge
Architecture
Product decisions
Acceptance decisions

          ↓ delegate

WORK + CODEX
────────────────────────────
Read 100 files
Inspect repo
Run tests
Compare implementation
Build evidence
Create artifacts
Execute bounded work
Git operations

          ↓ evidence

YOU + CHAT
────────────────────────────
Review findings
Challenge them
Learn
Decide
Approve/reject
```

And **later**, if Dot becomes available to you:

```text
                YOU
                 │
          judgement / direction
                 │
        ┌────────▼────────┐
        │      DOT        │
        │ ongoing owner   │
        └────────┬────────┘
                 │
       coordinates/delegates
          ┌──────┴──────┐
          ▼             ▼
        WORK          CODEX
     big tasks       repo/code
          └──────┬──────┘
                 ▼
          Git + evidence
                 │
                 ▼
              YOU/CHAT
          judgement/review
```

## My conclusion for **your actual situation**

**Don't replace Chat with Work. Don't replace your Git protocol with Dot.**

The useful change is:

**Stop using you as the workflow engine.**

You shouldn't have to keep saying *continue*, manually carry context between pages, repeatedly remind an AI to inspect Git, or babysit 20 mechanical review steps.

Let **Work/Codex do the labour**.

Keep **Chat + you for thinking, teaching, challenge and decisions**.

Eventually use **Dot for ongoing coordination**, provided we force the important state into Git/artifacts rather than trusting Dot's memory or its statement that something is “done.”

That is a genuine improvement over what we're doing today. **It is not a replacement for the valuable part of what we're doing today.** memcite
